title: Risk scenario
description: The join between controls and risk. A control with no scenario is unpriced - either find its scenario or ask why the control exists. Scenarios here carry STRUCTURE and no numbers: nothing in this repository has the loss data or the control measurement to quantify them yet, and a range with no provenance must not look as authoritative as one with six sourced parameters. The quantification hooks are declared and left null rather than guessed.

scenario_id.description: scn.<class>.<specific>. Referenced by control records; the validator refuses a control pointing at a scenario that does not exist here.

loss_event.description: The loss event itself, stated so that a frequency could be counted against it. Not a hazard and not a control gap - 'CUI is exfiltrated from the enclave' is a loss event; 'MFA is missing' is a control deficiency and belongs on a control record instead.

threat_community.description: Who or what acts. Named specifically enough that Threat Capability could be estimated against it later.

effect.description: Which security objective the loss event lands on. Several is normal.

loss_forms.description: Which loss forms are in play if this event occurs. Structure only - no magnitudes. Contractual and regulatory forms dominate in this domain, which is why they are named separately from the usual response and replacement costs.

quantification.description: Deliberately null until there is something to put here. Populating these from intuition is the failure this repository is built to avoid; they become computable once the pipeline has produced Variance Frequency and Variance Duration on the controls that serve this scenario.
